<!--
Shared partial: how the Compute layer of a practical unit is scheduled.

Included at the top of every unit's Compute section. IDENTICAL WORDING
EVERYWHERE ON PURPOSE -- students meet it once per unit and it must read as one
rule rather than as a different rule each session. That is the whole reason it
is a partial and not a paragraph.

WHY IT EXISTS. Measured on a real module: the opening demonstration plus the Do
and Interrogate layers fill a three-hour session, leaving under an hour, while
six to eight small functions with tests is 80-100 minutes for students at this
level. Every unit came out 20-30 minutes over, from the same cause. Saying
plainly that the Compute layer continues outside the session costs about two
hours across a whole practical, against the ~120 h of self-study a 6 ECTS module
budgets against ~60 h of contact.

It is also the better order pedagogically, which is why it is framed as a design
choice and not an apology: each Compute layer is built around one trap, the trap
is where having someone to ask matters, and the tests are a specification precise
enough to work against alone afterwards.

THE HEADING OF THE COMPUTE SECTION SHOULD CARRY THE TIMING TOO --
"## Layer 2 — Compute (start here, finish before the next session)" -- because a
student reading top to bottom reads headings, not callouts.

PATH CONVENTION: see /shared/partials/poll.qmd. Project-root-absolute paths only.
-->

::: {.callout-note title="Start this here, finish it before the next session"}
You are not expected to complete this during the session, and the session is not
timed on the assumption that you will.

**Start it here**, while there is someone to ask. Each of these exercises is built
around one place where the obvious implementation is quietly wrong, and that is the
part worth having help for.

**Finish it before the next session.** The tests are a complete specification —
they say exactly what each function must do — so you can work against them on your
own once you are past the awkward part. The next unit assumes this one's code
exists.

If you get stuck for more than about twenty minutes on the same thing, that is an
obstacle. Write it in the log and bring it.
:::

**Read Layer 3 before you leave, even though you will answer it later.** Some of
its questions are answered with numbers this layer produces, so they cannot all be
finished in the room either — but they tell you **what to look at while the data
is still in front of you**, and some of what they ask about is much harder to
recover once the session is over.
